Hi Samuel,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about FinBank's use cases and regulatory constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of needs (as discussed)
- Primary requirement: EU data residency for customer PII and transaction logs (must remain in EU data centers)
- Latency: sub-80ms p90 from major EU branches (Frankfurt/Paris) for inference paths
- Isolation: preference for private networking (VPC) or dedicated capacity for regulated workloads
- Compliance: SOC 2 + audit logs, KMS for key management, and (optionally) air-gapped on-prem for very sensitive flows

Options we discussed
1) Hosted API (EU region) – fastest to get started, can pin region to EU and avoid cross-region routing for standard traffic. Good for lower-risk data but may not meet stricter KMS/customer-managed key requirements.
2) Redwood Dedicated – reserved GPU pools in EU, predictable throughput and stronger tenant isolation. Control plane remains managed by Redwood, but data residency and audit logging are available.
3) Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) – customer-managed VPC with optional on-prem package. Offers customer KMS/HSM integration, full audit log retention, and no cross-tenant exposure. Recommended for regulated production workloads.

Open items / next steps
- We should schedule a technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions engineer) and Neha (sales engineer) to go through network diagrams, KMS options, and latency testing approach.
- I'll send the EU residency overview and our SOC 2 summary for your security team to review (attached).
- Please share any security questionnaire (if you have one) — we’ll have our compliance team fill that out.

Proposed times for a technical deep-dive: Mon Nov 30 10:00–11:00 CET or Tue Dec 1 14:00–15:00 CET. Let me know which works and I'll send an invite.

Attachments: Redwood-EU-Residency-Overview.pdf (overview of region availability, routing, and Private vs Dedicated tradeoffs)

Looking forward — thanks!

Cheers,
Aditya Rao

Hi Samuel — great questions. Answering inline: 

1) Hosted API EU residency
- Yes: our Hosted API offers EU-only region deployment model. Current GA regions for EU are eu-west-1 (Dublin) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). You can pin traffic to a single EU region; by default we do not route request or logs outside the pinned region unless you configure cross-region failover.
- Note: Hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS keys by default. Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private only.

2) Dedicated capacity (EU)
- Control plane: Redwood manages the control plane. Data plane (inference) runs in dedicated GPU pools located in the region you choose. You can enforce in-region routing for inference and logs. Dedicated gives stronger tenancy isolation and predictable SLAs, but it's still a managed offering.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations and full VPC peering (or on-prem appliance). We’ll share architecture diagrams in the deep-dive; Marissa will walk through the network/KMS options.

4) Latency
- Typical p90s (eu-central-1 / Frankfurt): 45–75ms from major EU metro regions depending on branch network; London is similar range. We’ll run an endpoint latency test during the deep-dive and can provide a trace.

Next steps
- Marissa / Neha — can you take the security questionnaire and draft answers for the items on KMS, audit logs, and region guarantees?
- Samuel — I’ll send the EU residency overview and a short pricing ballpark in a follow-up email (attaching initial ballpark).
- Schedule: I can do Mon Nov 30 10:00 CET — I’ll send a calendar invite for that slot; please let me know if you prefer Tue Dec 1.
